_comment: The permission a Workbench conversation asks for when its coding agent cannot reach mChatAI+ yet (2026-10-29). In the mchatai.com download the bridge (Settings > Coding Assistant > Allow terminal commands) is off until the person turns it on, and nothing told them it existed: an assistant could not read the page beside the chat, let alone propose clicks. Lawrence: 'It should just be another permission that pops up shouldn't it?' This is the pop-up. Shown only in builds that can serve the bridge (never the App Store build), until the person allows it or says not now; 'not now' is for good, and Settings stays the way back.
_honesty: Allow turns on the same setting as Settings > Allow terminal commands, which lets programs on this Mac send commands to mChatAI+. The copy says so. It must never claim more than the card system guarantees: clicks on a web page wait for the person's OK, either on the card or through a site they chose to always allow.
headline: Let {feature} use mChatAI+?
why: {feature} runs Claude Code or Codex, which reach mChatAI+ through terminal commands. Allow them, and your assistant can read the page beside the chat, use your applets, and suggest clicks on a web page. Nothing is clicked until you approve it.
note: This lets programs on this Mac send commands to mChatAI+. You can change it any time in Settings, under Coding Assistant.
